objective: Implement ADR-001 Phase 2: finish moving artifact-acceptance authority into the repository-scoped workflow core; extend governance-hook liveness enforcement from init to mid-run transitions; and introduce two human-gated, in-governance recovery paths: 'wf accept' for a schema-valid but unaccepted (stranded) artifact, and 'wf clear-invocation' for an orphaned open_invocation that otherwise deadlocks every transition including ESCALATED. No JSON Schema changes and no state-shape changes beyond a test-only heartbeat seed; all 34 existing governance tests stay green and 12 new regression tests are introduced, for a final suite of 46 tests.

in: Item 1: extract the accept pipeline (existence, then schema, then blocked-status, then semantic cross-checks, then counter bumps, then current-pointer update, then freeze, then ledger) out of the SubagentStop validator hook into a new pure core module gmdw/accept.py, leaving the SubagentStop validator a thin adapter. Behavior-preserving.

Item 1: delete the dead duplicate _subject_matches from the SubagentStop validator (the live copy in the gmdw state module, used by guard(), is the single remaining home); do NOT copy it into accept.py (the accept pipeline never calls it).
Item 3: introduce a human-gated 'wf accept --by <human>' recovery subcommand in the wf CLI, modeled on cmd_approve, reusing the item-1 core pipeline; it recovers a stranded ARTIFACT.

Item 3 (F1 recovery): introduce a human-gated 'wf clear-invocation --by <human>' recovery subcommand in the wf CLI that releases a confirmed-dead open_invocation, logs a distinct 'invocation_cleared' ledger event with actor 'human_recovery', and refuses cleanly when there is no open_invocation; it recovers an orphaned INVOCATION so ESCALATED / FAILED / REJECTED and normal transitions become reachable again.
Item 2: introduce a transition-time liveness re-check in the wf CLI cmd_transition, with a new hook-sourced-ledger-event read helper in the gmdw ledger module and a heartbeat-freshness fallback.

Item 2: reconcile the bypass env-var naming by introducing GMDW_ALLOW_UNGOVERNED as the canonical bypass honored by both init and transition, keeping GMDW_ALLOW_UNGOVERNED_INIT working at init for backward compatibility.

Item 4: introduce Phase-2 regression tests (wf accept happy and negative paths, wf clear-invocation recovery and negative paths, mid-run transition refusal and audited bypass, and a fail-closed validator-wrapper test), seed a fresh heartbeat in the test-suite Base.setUp so existing transition tests represent a governed session, and keep the full suite green through the thin hook.
Item 5: update docs (KNOWN_LIMITATIONS R4/F1, the gmdw command doc) and set the two ADR-001 document statuses to Accepted / Implemented, stating precisely what is closed.
out: No JSON Schema changes: the nine schema files under the workflow schemas directory remain untouched.
No state-shape changes except the test-only heartbeat seed in Base.setUp; the transition table is unchanged.

Reordering guard()'s ESCALATED allowance ahead of its open_invocation check (a state-core change) is NOT taken. The narrower, lower-risk reading is chosen: the orphaned-invocation deadlock is resolved by the human-gated 'wf clear-invocation' CLI recovery, leaving guard()'s single-flight ordering intact for normal transitions. The human plan gate may prefer the guard reorder instead; it is recorded here as the excluded alternative.
Run-ID recycling on pruned run directories (deferred by the request and ADR).
The GIT_STRATEGY versus LIVE_VALIDATION documentation drift about committing run folders (deferred).
The trivial-route human-gate question independent of hook liveness (deferred).

Phase-1 advisory findings other than the two the request pulls in: F-2, F-3, F-4, F-5, F-6, F-7 are NOT handled here. Only F-1 (future-skew bound, already fixed and carried forward) and F-8 (bypass naming reconciliation) are in scope.

An optional PreToolUse Bash rule denying 'wf accept' and 'wf clear-invocation' while hooks show live is NOT introduced here; it is flagged to the Security Reviewer (F5) as possible defense-in-depth, not required by this plan.

milestones.description: Extract the accept pipeline into a new pure core module gmdw/accept.py and reduce the SubagentStop validator hook to a thin adapter. Core entry point contract: accept_artifact(root, st, atype, version, *, actor=None) returns a Result object carrying outcome in {accepted, rejected, blocked, integrity_hold}, a reason string, a ledger event name for the failure cases (artifact_missing / artifact_invalid / artifact_rejected), and an extra dict (e.g. path, errors). NOTE (F4): there is NO rerun_tests parameter; _semantic continues to read verify.rerun_tests from st internally (prof = st policy snapshot; verify = prof verification), exactly as today. WHAT MOVES INTO CORE: the existence check, JSON parse and schemas.validate_artifact, blocked-status detection, the full _semantic() function (including its two subprocess calls: git merge-base ancestry and the shell test-rerun) moved VERBATIM, and the acceptance-plane mutations and side effects (the plan_revisions / impl_revisions / review_cycles and per-review counter bumps, setting st current[atype]=version, the freeze that marks the artifact read-only and records its sha256 in the registry, and the 'artifact_accepted' ledger event which includes an actor field only when a non-None actor is supplied so the hook path stays byte-identical). CORE SAVE CONTRACT (F4, be precise): the core does NOT call S.save_state and emits no block/ok, with exactly ONE intentional exception: _semantic's integrity-hold branch (today at subagentstop_validate.py:161-171) itself calls S.save_state and logs 'integrity_violation' then 'verification' on the test-rerun path. That in-core save-and-log is preserved verbatim and MUST NOT be normalized away, or tests 13 and 13b break. WHAT STAYS IN THE ADAPTER (session / hook-protocol plane): block()/ok(), _fail(), the open_invocation-then-last_invocation resolution, the consecutive_failures counter, the open_invocation lifecycle (retained on reject per test P6, cleared on accept and on blocked), the acceptance S.save_state call, the 'artifact_blocked' / 'artifact_missing' / 'artifact_invalid' / 'artifact_rejected' ledger writes, and the top-level fail-closed exception wrapper that sets flags.integrity_hold and logs 'validator_error'. Adapter Result mapping (must reproduce today's on-disk state and ledger exactly): accepted then set consecutive_failures=0, clear open_invocation, S.save_state, ok(); rejected then _fail (bump consecutive_failures, retain open_invocation, save, log the returned event, block(reason)); blocked then clear open_invocation, save, log 'artifact_blocked', block(reason); integrity_hold then treat as rejected exactly as today (the integrity_hold flag and 'integrity_violation' event were already written inside core, then _fail bumps consecutive_failures, logs 'artifact_rejected', block(reason)). Delete the dead _subject_matches from the SubagentStop validator (called nowhere in that file); the live copy in the state module used by guard() is the single home. The state module is NOT modified in this milestone. This is a pure, behavior-preserving refactor and MUST land alone before any new capability.
milestones.verification: Run 'python3 tests/test_governance.py' and verify it exits 0 reporting 34 tests OK, driving the extracted core through the thin hook. The behavioral oracle is the existing acceptance suite: tests P3, P5, P6, 13 and 13b must each pass unchanged (P5 pins open_invocation preference over last_invocation; P6 pins open_invocation retention on rejection; P3/13/13b pin accept, schema and semantic behavior). Static check: a search for _subject_matches in the SubagentStop validator returns no match; ast.parse of accept.py and of the SubagentStop validator both succeed.

milestones.description: Introduce the human-gated 'wf accept' recovery subcommand in the wf CLI, modeled structurally on cmd_approve, plus its five-plus-one regression tests. Argparse: a new 'accept' subparser with required '--by' (human attribution, matching approve) and an optional '--workflow'. cmd_accept behavior: load state; compute exp = S.expected(root, st); if exp is None (a state that produces no artifact, e.g. terminal or approval states) refuse cleanly with a CLI error and change nothing. Accept ONLY the exact artifact exp names for the current state: atype = exp artifact_type and version = exp version (S.expected computes the next version, st current.get(atype,0)+1, never an already-accepted one). Resolve run_rel = S.artifact_relpath(atype, version) and full = S.workflow_dir(root, wf_id) joined with run_rel. Refuse if the file is absent, or if ledger.is_frozen(root, wf_id, run_rel) is true (already accepted). Then call accept_artifact(root, st, atype, version, actor='human_recovery'): on a non-accepted outcome, refuse via the CLI error path with the returned reason and change NO state; on accepted, the core has already bumped counters, set st current[atype]=version, frozen the artifact and logged 'artifact_accepted' with actor='human_recovery' plus by=<--by value>; cmd_accept then sets consecutive_failures=0, clears open_invocation, calls S.save_state, and prints the accepted type and version. The distinct human_recovery actor and the by field keep audits able to separate hook-accepted from human-recovered artifacts. Tests (new class TestPhase2Recovery(Base)): test_R1_accept_unstrands_valid_repo_analysis (reproduce wf_20260713_003: a schema-valid repo_analysis_v1.json on disk with current.repo_analysis == 0; wf accept --by advances the pointer to 1, freezes the artifact, writes an 'artifact_accepted' ledger event with actor 'human_recovery', CLEARS a dangling open_invocation (F6), and the previously blocked REPOSITORY_ANALYSIS-to-PLANNING transition then passes); test_R2_accept_rejects_schema_invalid_artifact; test_R3_accept_rejects_wrong_version (a version that is not S.expected's next version is refused with no state change); test_R4_accept_rejects_already_frozen; test_R5_accept_requires_by (missing --by exits non-zero, no change); test_R6_accept_refuses_when_expected_is_none (F6: in a state where S.expected returns None, wf accept refuses cleanly with no change).
milestones.verification: Run 'python3 tests/test_governance.py' and verify it exits 0 reporting 40 tests OK (34 pre-existing plus the 6 new methods test_R1..test_R6, all introduced in this milestone). Each negative test asserts the workflow state file and current pointers are unchanged after refusal. Manual smoke, read-only against a scratch repo: 'wf accept' with no --by exits non-zero (argparse required).

milestones.description: Introduce the human-gated 'wf clear-invocation' recovery subcommand (F1 primary mechanism) plus its three regression tests. RATIONALE (verified): guard() checks open_invocation at state.py:252 and returns 'an agent invocation is still open; cannot transition' BEFORE the ESCALATED allowance at state.py:256 and before any liveness exemption cmd_transition applies; PreToolUse single-flight (pretooluse_gate.py:171) blocks any new invocation; and wf accept clears open_invocation ONLY on a successful accept. So an interrupted invocation that leaves a dangling open_invocation with no recoverable expected-version artifact deadlocks every transition, including ESCALATED/FAILED/REJECTED. Argparse: a new 'clear-invocation' subparser with required '--by' (human attribution) and an optional '--workflow'. cmd_clear_invocation behavior: load state; if st open_invocation is falsy, refuse via the CLI error path (exit non-zero) with no state change and no ledger write; otherwise capture the dead invocation summary (agent, expected_type, version), set st open_invocation = None, call S.save_state, and log a distinct 'invocation_cleared' ledger event with actor='human_recovery', by=<--by value>, and the captured summary. SCOPE OF EFFECT (be precise): clear-invocation ONLY releases the single-flight lock; it does NOT touch counters (consecutive_failures untouched), does NOT advance any current pointer, and does NOT freeze or accept anything. After it runs, guard() no longer sees an open invocation, so 'wf transition ESCALATED' (and FAILED/REJECTED, and normal targets) become reachable again; the human then resolves the escalation via wf approve. Tests (in TestPhase2Recovery): test_R7_clear_invocation_unblocks_escalate (seed a dangling open_invocation with no recoverable artifact; assert wf transition ESCALATED is first refused by guard with the open-invocation reason; run wf clear-invocation --by; assert open_invocation is None, an 'invocation_cleared' event with actor 'human_recovery' is logged, and wf transition ESCALATED then succeeds); test_R8_clear_invocation_refuses_when_none (no open_invocation: exits non-zero, no state change, no ledger event); test_R9_clear_invocation_requires_by (missing --by exits non-zero, no change).
milestones.verification: Run 'python3 tests/test_governance.py' and verify it exits 0 reporting 43 tests OK (40 from M2 plus the 3 new methods test_R7..test_R9). Each negative test asserts state and pointers are unchanged. Static check: a search for 'clear-invocation' in the wf CLI shows the subparser and cmd_clear_invocation wired in; ast.parse of the wf CLI succeeds.

milestones.description: Introduce a mid-run transition-time liveness re-check plus its supporting ledger read helper, the bypass reconciliation, and the test-fixture heartbeat seed, plus its two regression tests. (a) In the gmdw ledger module introduce a read-side helper (the module is write-only today) that reads the decision log and reports whether a hook-sourced event appears since the workflow's last 'transition' event, e.g. hook_event_since_last_transition(root, wf_id) returning bool, using the CONFIRMED hook-sourced event allowlist (F3): 'invocation_requested' (pretooluse_gate.py:182), 'invocation_completed' (posttooluse_ledger.py:74), and 'invocation_failed' (posttooluse_ledger.py:69). 'artifact_accepted' is deliberately EXCLUDED because the CLI writes it too (state.py:484-486 with actor='orchestrator', and now wf accept), so it cannot prove a hook fired. (b) In the wf CLI cmd_transition, before calling S.transition, when a workflow is ACTIVE and the target state a.to is not one of ESCALATED / FAILED / REJECTED (recovery/abandon exits stay exempt), compute liveness as: live if ledger.hook_event_since_last_transition(root, wf_id) is true OR heartbeat.status(root)[0] is true. heartbeat.status already carries the F-1 future-skew bound (MAX_FUTURE_SKEW_SEC=60), so the bound is inherited. If not live and not bypassed, refuse via the CLI error path with a diagnostic naming the real cause (governance hooks are not firing in this session) parallel to the init refusal and referencing the override, and log a 'transition_denied' ledger event (from_state, to_state, reason) so the mid-run refusal leaves an audit trail. (c) Bypass reconciliation (F-8): honor GMDW_ALLOW_UNGOVERNED (the canonical name the ADR prescribes) at transition, using the same truthiness read pattern as init; also accept a '--allow-ungoverned' flag on the transition subparser; on any bypass while ACTIVE log 'governance_liveness_bypassed' (reason, actor) mirroring init. Keep GMDW_ALLOW_UNGOVERNED_INIT honored at init, and additionally let init honor GMDW_ALLOW_UNGOVERNED so the canonical name works everywhere. (d) Seed a fresh heartbeat in the test-suite Base.setUp (after S.create_workflow) via heartbeat.touch(self.tmp, 'test-fixture') so the existing self.wf('transition', ...) calls in TestLimits / TestArtifacts / TestSecurityAndDeploy represent a governed session and pass the new check; document the seed with a comment. The state module and the heartbeat module are NOT modified. Tests (in TestPhase2Recovery): test_R10_transition_refuses_when_hooks_dark (ACTIVE workflow with the seeded heartbeat expired or removed AND no hook-sourced ledger event since the last transition: wf transition to a non-exempt state is refused with the liveness diagnostic and a 'transition_denied' ledger event, and state is unchanged); test_R11_transition_bypass_proceeds_and_logs (same dark condition, with GMDW_ALLOW_UNGOVERNED set or --allow-ungoverned given, the transition proceeds and a 'governance_liveness_bypassed' event is logged; also assert a transition to ESCALATED is NOT subject to the liveness check).
milestones.verification: Run 'python3 tests/test_governance.py' and verify it exits 0 reporting 45 tests OK (43 from M3 plus the 2 new methods test_R10..test_R11); all existing TestLimits / TestArtifacts / TestSecurityAndDeploy transition tests still pass because Base.setUp now seeds a heartbeat. Static check: ast.parse of the ledger module succeeds and a search for GMDW_ALLOW_UNGOVERNED in the wf CLI shows the canonical name wired into both init and transition.

milestones.description: Consolidated green-gate milestone that also lands the fail-closed validator-wrapper test the reviewer asked for (F6/AC3). Introduce test_R12_validator_error_sets_integrity_hold in TestPhase2Recovery: drive the real SubagentStop validator against a valid, expected artifact but with a deterministic internal fault injected on disk (recommended: corrupt the run's artifacts_index.json to non-JSON so freeze inside the accept path raises during registry load, which is past schema and semantic checks and inside main()'s body), then assert the top-level exception wrapper set flags.integrity_hold, logged a 'validator_error' event, and emitted a block decision. The implementor may substitute any equally deterministic disk-level fault that makes the accept path raise after the schema/semantic stage. This milestone runs the full suite as the refactor-safety gate: the extraction (M1), both recovery commands (M2/M3), and the mid-run liveness re-check (M4) must all be green together through the thin hook and the new commands. No production behavior changes here beyond the single new test.
milestones.verification: Run 'python3 tests/test_governance.py' and verify it exits 0 reporting 46 tests OK (the 34 pre-existing tests all present and passing, plus the 12 new methods test_R1..test_R12). Verify by name that test_R12_validator_error_sets_integrity_hold is collected and passes and that test_13 (integrity-hold via test-rerun mismatch) still passes.

milestones.description: Documentation and ADR status updates only (no code). In the KNOWN_LIMITATIONS doc update the R4 and F1 rows to state PRECISELY what is now closed and to record the residual, replacing the 'Mid-run hook loss is not yet caught, see Phase 2' wording. State that R4/F1 is closed via four mechanisms: (1) init refusal (Phase 1); (2) a mid-run transition liveness re-check; (3) stranded-artifact recovery via 'wf accept --by'; and (4) orphaned-invocation recovery via 'wf clear-invocation --by'. Record the residual explicitly: --by is trusted, not verified, and an optional PreToolUse deny of the two recovery commands while hooks show live is deferred (flagged to the Security Reviewer); guard()'s single-flight ordering is intentionally left unchanged and orphaned invocations are cleared by human recovery rather than auto-bypassed. Do NOT claim closure beyond these four mechanisms. In the gmdw command doc insert a note that transitions verify governance-hook liveness mid-run (with the GMDW_ALLOW_UNGOVERNED / --allow-ungoverned audited override), that 'wf accept --by <human>' is the human recovery path for a stranded, validly-produced artifact, and that 'wf clear-invocation --by <human>' is the human recovery path for an orphaned open_invocation. Set the ADR-001 phase2-plan doc status to Accepted / Implemented and the ADR-001 acceptance-and-liveness doc status from Proposed to Accepted / Implemented.
milestones.verification: Manual read: a search for 'wf accept' and 'clear-invocation' in the gmdw command doc each return a match; the R4/F1 rows in the KNOWN_LIMITATIONS doc no longer say mid-run is Phase 2 and enumerate the four closure mechanisms plus the residual; both ADR files show an Accepted/Implemented status line. No code behavior changes; 'python3 tests/test_governance.py' still exits 0 with 46 tests.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The full governance suite passes unchanged after the item-1 extraction: 'python3 tests/test_governance.py' exits 0 reporting 34 tests OK with all acceptance mechanics driven through the new gmdw/accept.py via the thin adapter, and the oracle tests P3, P5, P6, 13, 13b each pass.

accept.py exposes accept_artifact(root, st, atype, version, *, actor=None) (no rerun_tests parameter) returning a Result with outcome in {accepted, rejected, blocked, integrity_hold}, and the SubagentStop validator no longer defines _subject_matches (dead copy removed) while the state module's copy is retained and still used by guard().

The SubagentStop hook still fails closed: an internal error while a workflow is ACTIVE sets flags.integrity_hold and logs 'validator_error' (pinned by new test_R12), and a test-rerun mismatch still sets integrity_hold, logs 'integrity_violation', bumps consecutive_failures and blocks (pinned by test_13), exactly as before the refactor; _semantic's in-core save-and-log at the integrity branch is preserved verbatim (F4).

test_R1_accept_unstrands_valid_repo_analysis passes: with a schema-valid repo_analysis_v1.json on disk and current.repo_analysis == 0, 'wf accept --by <human>' advances current.repo_analysis to 1, freezes the artifact, writes an 'artifact_accepted' ledger event with actor 'human_recovery', clears a dangling open_invocation, and the REPOSITORY_ANALYSIS-to-PLANNING transition subsequently succeeds.

'wf accept' refuses and changes no state for: a schema-invalid artifact (test_R2), a version that is not S.expected's next version (test_R3), an already-frozen artifact (test_R4), a missing --by argument (test_R5 exits non-zero), and a state where S.expected returns None (test_R6).

Orphaned-invocation recovery (F1): with a dangling open_invocation and no recoverable expected-version artifact, 'wf transition ESCALATED' is first refused by guard(), then 'wf clear-invocation --by <human>' sets open_invocation to None, logs an 'invocation_cleared' event with actor 'human_recovery', touches no counters or pointers, and the ESCALATED transition then succeeds (test_R7); wf clear-invocation refuses with no state change and no ledger write when there is no open_invocation (test_R8) and exits non-zero when --by is missing (test_R9).

test_R10_transition_refuses_when_hooks_dark passes: with the heartbeat stale/absent and no hook-sourced ledger event since the last transition, a 'wf transition' to a non-exempt state is refused with a diagnostic naming governance-hook liveness and a 'transition_denied' ledger event is written, state unchanged; and test_R11_transition_bypass_proceeds_and_logs passes: under the same dark condition, GMDW_ALLOW_UNGOVERNED or --allow-ungoverned lets the transition proceed and logs 'governance_liveness_bypassed', while transitions to ESCALATED / FAILED / REJECTED are never subject to the liveness check.

The ledger module gains a read-side helper reporting whether a hook-sourced event (allowlist exactly {invocation_requested, invocation_completed, invocation_failed}, excluding artifact_accepted) appears since the last 'transition' event; cmd_transition treats the workflow as live if that helper is true OR heartbeat.status()[0] is true.

Bypass naming is reconciled: GMDW_ALLOW_UNGOVERNED is honored by both 'wf init' and 'wf transition', GMDW_ALLOW_UNGOVERNED_INIT continues to work at init, and Base.setUp seeds a fresh heartbeat so all pre-existing transition tests still pass.

The complete suite 'python3 tests/test_governance.py' exits 0 reporting 46 tests OK (34 pre-existing preserved plus 12 new test_R1..test_R12); no schema file under the workflow schemas directory is modified and no state-shape field is introduced beyond the test-only heartbeat seed.

Docs updated: the KNOWN_LIMITATIONS R4/F1 rows state precisely what is closed (init refusal, mid-run liveness re-check, stranded-artifact recovery via wf accept, and orphaned-invocation recovery via wf clear-invocation) and record the residual (--by trusted not verified; optional PreToolUse deny deferred; guard ordering unchanged), without claiming closure beyond those mechanisms; the gmdw command doc mentions wf accept, wf clear-invocation, and mid-run liveness verification; both ADR-001 documents show an Accepted/Implemented status.

risks.risk: Behavioral drift while extracting the most safety-critical code in the repo (the accept pipeline), e.g. a reordered save/freeze, a lost counter bump, or an altered ledger event shape.
risks.mitigation: Land item 1 as a pure, behavior-preserving refactor ALONE, gated on the existing 34-test oracle (P3/P5/P6/13/13b named) being green before any new capability is introduced. Move _semantic verbatim including its internal integrity-hold save-and-log (F4) rather than normalizing it. Keep the artifact_accepted event free of an actor field on the hook path.

risks.risk: The thin adapter drops the top-level fail-closed exception wrapper, turning a broken accept into a fail-open acceptance.
risks.mitigation: Keep the try/except wrapper (integrity_hold plus 'validator_error' plus block) in the SubagentStop validator main guard around the adapter; new test_R12 (F6) pins that it still engages.

risks.risk: 'wf accept' and 'wf clear-invocation' are new code-level, Bash-callable authorities more powerful than 'wf approve': accept advances current[atype], bumps counters and freezes; clear-invocation releases the single-flight lock. A misbehaving orchestrator could call them in a live session to self-accept a valid-but-ungoverned artifact or to escape single-flight while an agent is running.
risks.mitigation: wf accept runs the identical core validation (an invalid artifact is rejected either way), accepts ONLY S.expected's exact next-version artifact, refuses already-frozen artifacts, and records the distinct human_recovery actor; wf clear-invocation touches no counters/pointers/freeze and PreToolUse single-flight still governs the NEXT invocation. Both require human --by attribution as the compensating control. An optional PreToolUse deny of both while hooks show live is flagged to the Security Reviewer (F5), not adjudicated here.

risks.risk: Seeding a heartbeat in Base.setUp could mask a genuine liveness regression because every legacy test then sees a fresh beacon.
risks.mitigation: Dedicated tests (test_R10/test_R11) explicitly expire or remove the heartbeat and clear hook-sourced ledger events to exercise the refusal and bypass paths directly.

risks.risk: The shell test-rerun boundary (a subprocess with shell=True from the artifact-declared command) is now reachable from the CLI when a human runs 'wf accept' against a stranded implementation manifest.
risks.mitigation: This is the same already-accepted trust boundary the hook uses; it is gated on human --by attribution and only runs the exact expected artifact. Documented as an inherited surface, not a new one; noted for the Security Reviewer (F5).

risks.risk: Circular import between accept.py and the state module.
risks.mitigation: accept.py imports the state module (as S), the ledger module and the schemas module; the state module does NOT import accept. The cmd_transition liveness lives in the wf CLI and the ledger module, not in the state module, so the state module is unchanged.

assumptions: pytest is not installed in this environment; the authoritative oracle is 'python3 tests/test_governance.py' (stdlib unittest), which currently reports 34 tests OK (verified this session).
current.plan == 1 for wf_20260714_001 (verified via the run state), so this plan artifact is version 2 (plan_v2.json), the exact next version S.expected() names.

guard() checks open_invocation at state.py:252 and returns BEFORE the ESCALATED allowance at state.py:256 (verified), so a dangling open_invocation blocks every transition including the recovery exits; the F1 fix is the human-gated 'wf clear-invocation' CLI command, and guard()'s ordering is intentionally NOT changed.

The hook-sourced allowlist is confirmed (F3): 'invocation_requested' (pretooluse_gate.py:182), 'invocation_completed' (posttooluse_ledger.py:74), 'invocation_failed' (posttooluse_ledger.py:69); 'artifact_accepted' is excluded because the CLI writes it (state.py:484-486, actor='orchestrator', and now wf accept). The prior 'unverified event names' risk is retired.

_semantic's integrity-hold branch (subagentstop_validate.py:161-171) calls S.save_state and logs 'integrity_violation' then 'verification' on the test-rerun path; this is the ONE intentional in-core save-and-log and is preserved verbatim; there is no rerun_tests parameter on accept_artifact (F4).

wf accept resets consecutive_failures to 0 and clears open_invocation on a successful recovery (mirroring hook acceptance); wf clear-invocation only clears open_invocation and touches no other state field. Neither is a state-shape change.

wf accept and wf clear-invocation trust the --by value (human attribution); it is not cryptographically verified. Confining them via a PreToolUse deny while hooks show live is deferred to the Security Reviewer (F5).
The new GMDW_ALLOW_UNGOVERNED bypass uses the same truthiness read pattern as the existing GMDW_ALLOW_UNGOVERNED_INIT for consistency; hardening the truthiness check (Phase-1 F-4) is out of scope.
The liveness re-check is placed in the wf CLI cmd_transition (not in state.transition), consistent with Phase 1 placing the init check in cmd_init and keeping the state core as pure mechanism.

Transitions to ESCALATED / FAILED / REJECTED are exempt from the liveness check; combined with wf clear-invocation, recovery and abandon exits are reachable once any dangling open_invocation is cleared.
heartbeat.status() already carries the F-1 future-skew bound (MAX_FUTURE_SKEW_SEC=60) and is reused unchanged; the heartbeat module is not modified.
No new or changed artifact schema is required; all nine schema files remain untouched.

dependencies.detail: 'wf accept' and 'wf clear-invocation' each require a human --by attribution value at invocation time; they are recovery gates, not orchestrator-callable commands, in the same category as 'wf approve'.

files.reason: New pure, repository-scoped core module holding accept_artifact() and the moved _semantic() (with its git-ancestry and shell test-rerun checks); the single home of the accept pipeline, callable from both the hook and the CLI.

Reduce to a thin adapter: resolve the active invocation, call accept_artifact, translate the Result to block/ok and the session-plane mutations (consecutive_failures, open_invocation, the acceptance save_state); keep the fail-closed exception wrapper; delete the dead _subject_matches copy.

Introduce the 'wf accept --by' recovery subcommand and the 'wf clear-invocation --by' orphaned-invocation recovery subcommand (both reusing core primitives), and introduce the mid-run liveness re-check in cmd_transition with the GMDW_ALLOW_UNGOVERNED / --allow-ungoverned audited bypass and reconciled init bypass naming.

Introduce a read-side helper over the decision log reporting whether a hook-sourced event (allowlist invocation_requested / invocation_completed / invocation_failed) appears since the last 'transition' event (the module is write-only today); used by the cmd_transition liveness predicate.

Seed a fresh heartbeat in Base.setUp so existing transition tests represent a governed session; introduce the twelve Phase-2 regression tests (test_R1..test_R12) for wf accept, wf clear-invocation, mid-run transition liveness, and the fail-closed validator wrapper.
Update R4/F1 to record the four closure mechanisms (init, mid-run, wf accept, wf clear-invocation) and the residual, replacing the 'mid-run is Phase 2' note; do not overstate closure.

Document that transitions verify governance-hook liveness mid-run (with the audited override) and that 'wf accept --by' and 'wf clear-invocation --by' are the human recovery paths for a stranded artifact and an orphaned invocation respectively.
Set status to Accepted / Implemented once Phase 2 lands.
Set status from Proposed to Accepted / Implemented.

revision_notes.resolution: MAJOR resolved by scoping in a new human-gated in-governance recovery for orphaned invocations as a dedicated milestone (M3): 'wf clear-invocation --by <human>' releases a confirmed-dead open_invocation, logs a distinct 'invocation_cleared' ledger event with actor 'human_recovery', and refuses when there is no open_invocation. Chosen as the ONE primary mechanism (justified in scope.out): it keeps guard()'s state-core single-flight ordering intact for normal transitions while restoring reachability of ESCALATED/FAILED/REJECTED after a human clears the dead invocation; the guard-reorder alternative is recorded as the excluded reading. M3 has files, verification, acceptance criteria (AC6) and tests test_R7..test_R9 (test_R7 proves ESCALATED is first blocked by guard, then unblocked after clear). Closure wording corrected in M6/AC11 and the KNOWN_LIMITATIONS update: R4/F1 is stated as closed via exactly four mechanisms (init refusal, mid-run re-check, wf accept for stranded artifacts, wf clear-invocation for orphaned invocations), with the residual (--by trusted, optional PreToolUse deny deferred, guard ordering unchanged) recorded; no 'closed end-to-end' claim beyond those.

Test placement made explicit and monotonic. Each capability ships with its own tests: M2 introduces test_R1..test_R6 (suite 34 then 40); M3 introduces test_R7..test_R9 (43); M4 introduces test_R10..test_R11 (45); M5 introduces test_R12 and is the consolidated green gate (46). Every verification block now states the exact cumulative count for that milestone and no milestone references a test introduced later. The old contradictory 'at least 39' / 'from M4' wording is removed.

The confirmed hook-sourced allowlist {invocation_requested, invocation_completed, invocation_failed} is baked into M4, AC8 and the assumptions, with source lines (pretooluse_gate.py:182, posttooluse_ledger.py:74, posttooluse_ledger.py:69) and the explicit exclusion of artifact_accepted (state.py:484-486). The prior 'unverified event names' risk is retired (removed from risks).

The M1 core save contract is restated precisely: the core does NOT call S.save_state and emits no block/ok, with exactly ONE intentional exception — _semantic's integrity-hold branch (subagentstop_validate.py:161-171) which calls S.save_state and logs 'integrity_violation' then 'verification'; that in-core save-and-log is preserved verbatim and MUST NOT be normalized, or tests 13/13b break. The contradictory rerun_tests parameter is dropped: accept_artifact(root, st, atype, version, *, actor=None) and _semantic keeps reading verify.rerun_tests from st internally. AC2 and AC3 updated accordingly.

The security-relevant surface is recorded: wf accept and the new wf clear-invocation are new code-level, Bash-callable authorities more powerful than wf approve (accept advances pointers/counters and freezes; clear-invocation releases the single-flight lock). Captured in risks with compensating controls and in scope.out/assumptions as an option (not a requirement) for the Security Reviewer: an optional PreToolUse deny of both commands while hooks show live. Not adjudicated in this plan.

Named backing tests inserted: AC3 is pinned by new test_R12 (fail-closed validator-wrapper: integrity_hold set + 'validator_error' logged + block) and by existing test_13 (integrity-hold via test-rerun mismatch); test_R6 covers the wf accept clean refusal when S.expected returns None; and test_R1 (AC4) asserts a successful wf accept clears a dangling open_invocation.
